title: The Insane Story Behind the Ferrari Enzo

scenes.text: A car named after a dead man, sold only to people Ferrari chose, with a final example given to a Pope. That is the short version of the Ferrari Enzo. The long version is stranger: a road car built with Formula One technology that Formula One itself would not allow, whose numbers every source reports differently. This is the story behind the Ferrari Enzo, and where the tellers disagree.
scenes.caption: THE INSANE STORY BEHIND THE FERRARI ENZO

scenes.text: Our sources are Wikipedia's pages on the Enzo and the F50, RM Sotheby's catalogue pages for four different cars, Sports Car Market, Hagerty, the magazine evo, Jalopnik, the DuPont Registry and Italpassion. Where they conflict, we show both versions. Our own arithmetic is labelled, and what we could not find is flagged.
scenes.caption: SOURCES: WIKIPEDIA (ENZO, F50) · RM SOTHEBY'S (LONDON 2014, ARIZONA 2017, CALIFORNIA 2015, MONTEREY 2021) · SCM · HAGERTY · EVO · JALOPNIK · DUPONT REGISTRY · ITALPASSION · CONFLICTS SHOWN

scenes.text: Ferrari's previous hypercar, the F50, was not a hit. Sports Car Market says its production run of three hundred forty-nine was one car less than the market demanded, that first owners leased rather than bought, and that the F40 hit a hot button which the F50 simply missed. Jalopnik, in twenty ten, called the F50 the unloved middle child.
scenes.caption: SCM (F50 PROFILE): 349 BUILT, 'ONE LESS THAN THE MARKET DEMANDED'; FIRST OWNERS LEASED; 'THE F40 HIT A HOT BUTTON WHICH THE F50 SIMPLY MISSED' · JALOPNIK (13 JUL 2010): 'UNLOVED MIDDLE CHILD'
scenes.chapter: Before the Enzo: a hard act to follow

scenes.text: The F50 had still been a serious car. Ferrari's chairman, Luca di Montezemolo, told Motor Trend it would be the first and last Formula One car with two seats, RM Sotheby's reports. Wikipedia says the last F50 left the line in July nineteen ninety-seven. By our arithmetic, the Enzo was announced about five years and two months later.
scenes.caption: RM SOTHEBY'S (F50): MONTEZEMOLO — 'THE FIRST AND LAST FORMULA 1 CAR WITH TWO SEATS' · WIKIPEDIA (F50): LAST CAR JULY 1997 · WIKIPEDIA (ENZO): PARIS MOTOR SHOW 2002 (RM: SEPTEMBER) · JULY 1997 → SEPT 2002 = 5 YEARS 2 MONTHS (OUR ARITHMETIC)

scenes.text: In between, Ferrari's Formula One team was winning. RM Sotheby's Arizona catalogue credits the Enzo's Formula One link to Ferrari's manufacturers' championships in nineteen ninety-nine and two thousand and its drivers' championship in two thousand. The London catalogue says the team had just won its second consecutive drivers' and constructors' titles and was pursuing a third.
scenes.caption: RM SOTHEBY'S (ARIZONA 2017): FERRARI 1999 + 2000 MANUFACTURERS' CHAMPIONSHIPS; 2000 DRIVERS' CHAMPIONSHIP · RM SOTHEBY'S (LONDON 2014): TEAM 'HAD JUST WON ITS SECOND CONSECUTIVE' DRIVERS' + CONSTRUCTORS' TITLES, PURSUING A THIRD · THE TWO CATALOGUES USE DIFFERENT FRAMINGS

scenes.text: The Arizona catalogue adds that Michael Schumacher was just getting started on what it calls a still unequalled feat of five consecutive championships. That is the catalogue's framing, not a quote from Ferrari. It does not say Schumacher worked on the Enzo; Wikipedia only mentions him in connection with the later FXX track car. We cannot confirm any development role.
scenes.caption: RM SOTHEBY'S (ARIZONA 2017): SCHUMACHER 'JUST GETTING STARTED ON HIS HISTORIC DOMINANCE OF F1' · 'FIVE CONSECUTIVE CHAMPIONSHIPS' (CATALOGUE'S FRAMING) · WIKIPEDIA: SCHUMACHER MENTIONED FOR THE FXX (2009) ONLY · SCHUMACHER'S ROLE IN ENZO DEVELOPMENT: NOT IN OUR SOURCES

scenes.text: The name came from the top. RM Sotheby's says the car was named Enzo, not F60, per Montezemolo. Wikipedia says it is officially marketed as Enzo Ferrari. The Arizona catalogue says that in mid-two thousand two Montezemolo introduced the car as honouring the company's founder and as having a strong connection to Formula One.
scenes.caption: RM SOTHEBY'S (CA15): NAMED 'ENZO' INSTEAD OF 'F60', PER MONTEZEMOLO · WIKIPEDIA: 'OFFICIALLY MARKETED AS ENZO FERRARI' · RM SOTHEBY'S (ARIZONA 2017): INTRODUCED MID-2002 AS HONOURING THE FOUNDER, STRONG F1 LINK

scenes.text: The engine was new. The catalogue says the six litre Tipo F140 B was purpose-built for the car, and was the largest engine from Maranello since the seven twelve Can-Am race car. Wikipedia lists six hundred sixty metric horsepower. By our arithmetic, the car made a hundred ten metric horsepower per litre. The Can-Am car's size is not given in our sources.
scenes.caption: RM SOTHEBY'S (ARIZONA 2017 + LONDON 2014): TIPO F140 B 5,998 CC, PURPOSE-BUILT; 'LARGEST MARANELLO ENGINE SINCE THE 712 CAN-AM' · WIKIPEDIA: 660 PS · 660 ÷ 5.9988 = 110 PS/L (OUR ARITHMETIC) · 712 CAN-AM DISPLACEMENT: NOT IN OUR SOURCES

scenes.text: The structure was carbon. The Arizona catalogue says a carbon-fibre and Nomex honeycomb tub weighing about two hundred pounds carried aluminium sub-frames. By our arithmetic, that is about ninety-one kilograms. Wikipedia describes a carbon-fibre body too, plus carbon-ceramic brakes, and active aerodynamics that Formula One did not allow.
scenes.caption: RM SOTHEBY'S (ARIZONA 2017): CARBON + NOMEX TUB ~200 LB (= 90.7 KG, OUR ARITHMETIC) WITH ALUMINIUM SUB-FRAMES · WIKIPEDIA: CARBON-FIBRE BODY; C/SIC CERAMIC BRAKES; ACTIVE AERO 'WHICH F1 DID NOT ALLOW'

scenes.text: The shape came from Ken Okuyama, who Wikipedia names as Pininfarina's head of design at the time. The Arizona catalogue says Okuyama penned the exterior, Pininfarina built the coachwork, and the design was aerodynamically perfected in Pininfarina's wind tunnel. Wikipedia lists the downforce at three hundred forty-three kilograms at two hundred kilometres an hour.
scenes.caption: WIKIPEDIA: DESIGNED BY KEN OKUYAMA, PININFARINA HEAD OF DESIGN · RM (ARIZONA 2017): OKUYAMA PENNED EXTERIOR; PININFARINA BUILT COACHWORK; WIND-TUNNEL PERFECTED · WIKIPEDIA: DOWNFORCE 343 KG @ 200 KM/H, 775 KG @ 300, 585 KG AT TOP SPEED

scenes.text: The test cars were disguised. Wikipedia says three development mules, called M1, M2 and M3, used bodywork from the Ferrari three forty-eight. The third mule sold at auction in June two thousand five for one hundred ninety-five thousand five hundred euros, or two hundred thirty-six thousand three hundred dollars. By our arithmetic, that is thirty-seven percent of the Enzo's list price.
scenes.caption: WIKIPEDIA: MULES M1–M3 USED 348 BODYWORK · M3 SOLD JUNE 2005 €195,500 (US$236,300) · SCM LIST $643,330 · 236,300 ÷ 643,330 = 36.7% (OUR ARITHMETIC)

scenes.text: The gearbox was the headline. Wikipedia says it was an F1-style automated manual with paddle shifters, built by Graziano, shifting in one hundred fifty milliseconds. RM Sotheby's London page says the car was Ferrari's fastest road car at the time. But Wikipedia also notes the gearbox was a first-generation clutchless design with complaints about abrupt shifts.
scenes.caption: WIKIPEDIA: F1-STYLE AUTOMATED MANUAL, GRAZIANO, 150 MS; 'FIRST-GENERATION' WITH ABRUPT-SHIFT COMPLAINTS · RM (LONDON 2014): 'FERRARI'S FASTEST ROAD CAR AT THE TIME'

scenes.text: The Enzo was unveiled at the Paris Auto Show in September two thousand two, per RM Sotheby's. Wikipedia says it was announced at the two thousand two Paris show and does not give the month. Wikipedia also records a surprising earlier appearance: the actress Demi Moore drove an Enzo show car on a beach in Charlie's Angels: Full Throttle before the Paris unveiling.
scenes.caption: RM SOTHEBY'S: UNVEILED PARIS AUTO SHOW, SEPTEMBER 2002 · WIKIPEDIA: ANNOUNCED PARIS MOTOR SHOW 2002 (NO MONTH) · DEMI MOORE DROVE A SHOW CAR ON A BEACH IN CHARLIE'S ANGELS: FULL THROTTLE BEFORE THE UNVEILING (WIKIPEDIA; ONE LINE, NO DETAIL)

scenes.text: The reception was split. Sports Car International ranked it third among the top sports cars of the two thousands, and Motor Trend Classic ranked it fourth among the greatest Ferraris, Wikipedia says. But the same page notes Bloomberg Businessweek put it among the fifty ugliest cars. Jalopnik said in twenty ten that it had aged well and would not draw design complaints today.
scenes.caption: WIKIPEDIA: SPORTS CAR INTERNATIONAL #3 OF THE 2000s (2004) · MOTOR TREND CLASSIC #4 GREATEST FERRARIS · BLOOMBERG BUSINESSWEEK 'FIFTY UGLIEST' · JALOPNIK (13 JUL 2010): 'AGED WELL'

scenes.text: The performance numbers were contested from the start. Road and Track, via RM Sotheby's, recorded zero to sixty in three point three seconds. RM's London catalogue claims three point six. Wikipedia lists three point one four seconds, but measured downhill with a rollout, and Motor Trend's three point three. By our arithmetic, the catalogue's claim is nine percent slower than Road and Track's test.
scenes.caption: RM (CA15, R&T): 3.3 S · RM (LONDON 2014): 'CLAIMED' 3.6 S · WIKIPEDIA: 3.14 S (DOWNHILL, 1-FT ROLLOUT); MOTOR TREND 3.3 S · 3.6 ÷ 3.3 = +9.1% · 3.3 ÷ 3.14 = +5.1% (OUR ARITHMETIC)

scenes.text: Top speed was similar. Wikipedia says up to three hundred fifty-five kilometres an hour, which is two hundred twenty-one miles an hour, while RM Sotheby's and Sports Car Market say two hundred eighteen. RM's London page compares the car to the Porsche Carrera GT and the Mercedes-Benz SLR McLaren. Wikipedia says the Carrera GT was one point one seconds quicker at Bedford Autodrome.
scenes.caption: WIKIPEDIA: TOP SPEED UP TO 355 KM/H (221 MPH) · RM + SCM: 218 MPH · RM (LONDON 2014): COMPARED WITH PORSCHE CARRERA GT + MERCEDES-BENZ SLR MCLAREN · WIKIPEDIA: BEDFORD AUTODROME WEST 1:21.3, ~1.1 S SLOWER THAN THE CARRERA GT

scenes.text: You could not simply order an Enzo. RM Sotheby's London page says Ferrari invited only its best existing owners. The California page says buyers were generally owners of the F50 and F40. Wikipedia agrees that invitations went to F40 and F50 owners. By design, the people who had bought, or leased, the previous two cars got first call.
scenes.caption: RM (LONDON 2014): 'INVITED ONLY THEIR BEST EXISTING OWNERS' · RM (CA15): 'GENERALLY BUYERS OF THE F50 AND F40' · WIKIPEDIA: INVITATIONS TO F40 + F50 OWNERS

scenes.text: The numbers moved. RM says three hundred forty-nine cars were planned, all allocated before production began. After many client requests, Ferrari added fifty, for three hundred ninety-nine. Wikipedia says the run was announced as three hundred ninety-nine, and the Arizona catalogue says production was capped at four hundred, with three hundred ninety-nine going to customers and the last earmarked for the Pope.
scenes.caption: RM (LONDON 2014): 349 PLANNED, ALL ALLOCATED; 'AFTER MANY CLIENT REQUESTS' +50 = 399 · WIKIPEDIA: ANNOUNCED AS 399 · RM (ARIZONA 2017): CAPPED AT 400; 399 TO CUSTOMERS; 400TH FOR THE POPE · 349 + 50 = 399 (OUR ARITHMETIC)

scenes.text: Not everyone agrees on the total. Wikipedia's text says four hundred ninety-eight were built, while Hagerty, Sports Car Market and the PistonHeads listing say four hundred. Italpassion says four hundred ninety-eight, with one hundred eleven for the United States. By our arithmetic, the disputed difference is ninety-eight cars, and no source explains it.
scenes.caption: WIKIPEDIA + ITALPASSION: 498 · HAGERTY + SCM + PISTONHEADS: 400 · 498 − 400 = 98 (OUR ARITHMETIC) · REASON: NOT STATED · HAGERTY US: 80 vs ITALPASSION US: 111

scenes.text: One named first owner appears in our sources. RM Sotheby's Arizona catalogue says a two thousand three Enzo was delivered new to the fashion designer Tommy Hilfiger, through Miller Motorcars in Greenwich, Connecticut. The catalogue notes Hilfiger sponsored Scuderia Ferrari in the early two thousands and designed the drivers' uniforms. At a service in September twenty sixteen, it showed three thousand six hundred twenty miles.
scenes.caption: RM SOTHEBY'S (ARIZONA 2017): FIRST AND ONLY OWNER TOMMY HILFIGER (FASHION DESIGNER), DELIVERED VIA MILLER MOTORCARS, GREENWICH CT · HILFIGER SPONSORED SCUDERIA FERRARI IN EARLY 2000s; DESIGNED F1 DRIVERS' UNIFORMS · 3,620 MI AT SEPT 2016 SERVICE

scenes.text: By our arithmetic, that car covered about three thousand six hundred miles in thirteen years, an average of under three hundred miles a year. The catalogue sold it for two million six hundred ninety-five thousand dollars in Arizona in twenty seventeen, about four point two times the Enzo's list price of six hundred forty-three thousand three hundred thirty dollars.
scenes.caption: 3,620 MI IN ~13.5 YEARS (2003 → SEP 2016) = ~270 MI/YEAR · RM (ARIZONA 2017): $2,695,000 · 2,695,000 ÷ 643,330 = 4.2× (OUR ARITHMETIC; SALE DATE WITHIN 2017 NOT GIVEN)

scenes.text: The final car is the oddest part of the story. RM Sotheby's London says a four hundredth Enzo was presented to Pope John Paul II as a gift and later auctioned for charity on his behalf. The California page says it was built for him. Wikipedia says the four hundredth car was built in two thousand four and donated to the Vatican for charity.
scenes.caption: RM (LONDON 2014): 400TH 'PRESENTED TO POPE JOHN PAUL II AS A GIFT AND LATER AUCTIONED FOR CHARITY ON HIS BEHALF' · RM (CA15): 'BUILT FOR POPE JOHN PAUL II' · WIKIPEDIA: BUILT 2004, DONATED TO THE VATICAN FOR CHARITY

scenes.text: The charity is disputed. Wikipedia says the car later sold at Sotheby's for one point one million dollars. But its own cited sources reference a donation to St. Jude Children's Research Hospital, and carry a date of December two thousand five. By our arithmetic, one point one million dollars was one point seven times the list price. We cannot resolve the charity question.
scenes.caption: WIKIPEDIA: SOLD AT SOTHEBY'S FOR US$1.1 M · CITED SOURCES REFERENCE ST. JUDE CHILDREN'S RESEARCH HOSPITAL; DATED DEC 2005 · 1,100,000 ÷ 643,330 = 1.7× (OUR ARITHMETIC) · CHARITY / BUYER / SALE DATE: UNRESOLVED

scenes.text: Several details of the papal car are missing from our sources: the date it was handed over, the buyer, and the exact sale date. RM Sotheby's calls it a gift, Wikipedia says it was donated for charity, and the catalogue for the Arizona car says the four hundredth was earmarked for the Pope. We report each wording as it appears.
scenes.caption: RM (LONDON 2014): 'PRESENTED … AS A GIFT' · WIKIPEDIA: 'DONATED TO THE VATICAN FOR CHARITY' · RM (ARIZONA 2017): 'EARMARKED FOR THE POPE' · HANDOVER DATE, BUYER, SALE DATE: NOT IN OUR SOURCES

scenes.text: The Enzo spawned relatives. Wikipedia says Maserati built fifty MC12s from the Enzo's engine, chassis and gearbox, because racing homologation required twenty-five road cars. Ferrari's own FXX, loosely based on the Enzo, cost one point three million euros initially and stayed under Ferrari's control for use by selected clients on track. The program ran until two thousand nine.
scenes.caption: WIKIPEDIA: MASERATI MC12 (2004–05) — SAME ENGINE, CHASSIS, GEARBOX · 50 BUILT · 25 ROAD CARS FOR HOMOLOGATION · FXX (2005) €1.3 M, CLIENT TRACK USE, TO 2009

scenes.text: The most famous FXX moment involved Schumacher. Wikipedia says that in a two thousand nine Top Gear test, he set a lap of one minute ten point seven seconds in the FXX, wearing the Stig's white suit because Ben Collins was not a selected client. The record was later removed, because the car was not road-legal.
scenes.caption: WIKIPEDIA: FXX — SCHUMACHER 1:10.7, TOP GEAR 2009 · WORE THE STIG'S WHITE SUIT (BEN COLLINS NOT A SELECTED CLIENT) · RECORD REMOVED (NOT ROAD-LEGAL)

scenes.text: A one-off followed. Wikipedia says James Glickenhaus commissioned the Ferrari P four five by Pininfarina on the last unregistered US-specification Enzo chassis, keeping the Enzo's drivetrain and identification number. By our arithmetic, that means the unique car is, in law, an Enzo that was rebodied. The page does not discuss that legal question, so we just flag it.
scenes.caption: WIKIPEDIA: FERRARI P 4/5 BY PININFARINA (2006), COMMISSIONED BY JAMES GLICKENHAUS, LAST UNREGISTERED US-SPEC ENZO CHASSIS, KEEPS DRIVETRAIN + VIN · 'IN LAW AN ENZO' = OUR INFERENCE; LEGAL STATUS NOT DISCUSSED

scenes.text: For the first years, the Enzo sold for a premium. Wikipedia says the Pope's car made one point one million dollars. By two thousand fourteen, RM Sotheby's sold a one-owner car with under nineteen hundred kilometres in London for nine hundred fifty-two thousand pounds. We do not have a currency source to convert that, so we leave the pounds as pounds.
scenes.caption: WIKIPEDIA: 400TH CAR $1.1 M (CITED SOURCES DATE DEC 2005) · RM SOTHEBY'S LONDON 2014 (LOT 140): £952,000, <1,900 KM, ONE OWNER, CLASSICHE · NO EXCHANGE-RATE SOURCE → NOT CONVERTED

scenes.text: Then the money rose. RM Sotheby's California sale in twenty fifteen lists a two thousand four Enzo at one million eight hundred seventy thousand dollars. Arizona, twenty seventeen, two million six hundred ninety-five thousand. Sports Car Market reports two million five hundred thirty thousand seven hundred seventy-four in London in September twenty eighteen, including the buyer's premium, and a recent Mecum result of two million eight hundred sixty thousand, from Hagerty.
scenes.caption: RM CA15: $1,870,000 · RM ARIZONA 2017: $2,695,000 · SCM: $2,530,774 (RM LONDON, 15 SEP 2018, INCL. PREMIUM) · HAGERTY: $2,860,000 MECUM 16 AUG 2024 · SALES ARE DIFFERENT CARS WITH DIFFERENT MILEAGE

scenes.text: Hagerty now puts a good Enzo at three million six hundred thousand dollars, flat for twelve months. By our arithmetic, that is about five point six times the list price and three point three times the Pope's car. Italpassion lists a claimed record of six point oh five million dollars from Monterey in twenty fifteen, which conflicts with Hagerty's highest recorded sale of four million five hundred ten thousand.
scenes.caption: HAGERTY: $3,600,000 (#3 'GOOD'), 12-MONTH 0% · 3.6 ÷ 0.64333 = 5.6× · 3.6 ÷ 1.1 = 3.3× (OUR ARITHMETIC) · ITALPASSION RECORD $6.05 M (MONTEREY 2015) vs HAGERTY HIGH $4.51 M → CONFLICT

scenes.text: A January twenty twenty-six sale in Phoenix has an estimate of five to six million dollars for an Enzo with just seven hundred forty-six miles, Italpassion says. The same page puts a F50 at seven to nine million. We don't have the results. So the pre-sale numbers say collectors value a nearly unused Enzo far above Hagerty's typical figure, but those are guesses by the auction house.
scenes.caption: ITALPASSION (RM PHOENIX, 23 JAN 2026): ENZO 746 MI, ESTIMATE $5–6 M · F50 ESTIMATE $7–9 M · RESULTS: NOT IN OUR SOURCES · ESTIMATES = AUCTION HOUSE'S, NOT PRICES

scenes.text: There is a darker footnote. RM Sotheby's California page says that an alarming number of the four hundred have been written off by inexperienced or cavalier drivers, which makes well-kept examples more desirable. The page does not give a number, and our other sources do not either, so we cannot say how many survive.
scenes.caption: RM SOTHEBY'S (CA15): 'AN ALARMING NUMBER' OF THE 400 'WRITTEN OFF' BY 'INEXPERIENCED OR CAVALIER DRIVERS' · COUNT / SURVIVORS: NOT IN OUR SOURCES

scenes.text: A final data point on scarcity. Hagerty records only sixty-six sales of two thousand two to two thousand four Enzos, and six public auction sales of the two thousand three model in the last three years. By our arithmetic, that is two public sales a year. For a car with about four hundred built, that is a rare event, and every sale becomes news.
scenes.caption: HAGERTY: 66 SALES (2002–04 ENZO) · 6 PUBLIC AUCTION SALES (2003 MODEL, LAST 3 YEARS) = 2/YEAR (OUR ARITHMETIC) · ~400 BUILT · 'EVERY SALE BECOMES NEWS' = OUR OPINION

scenes.text: How does the Enzo rank against its siblings? Evo's February two thousand four group test put it third of four, behind the Ferrari two eighty-eight GTO and the F50, ahead of the F40. Bovingdon complained of no steering feel. Meaden said there is not enough to do except hang on and concentrate on braking points. The fastest of the four was not the favourite.
scenes.caption: EVO (BARKER; ISSUE 64, FEB 2004): 288 GTO > F50 > ENZO > F40 · BOVINGDON: 'STEERING FEEL, OF WHICH THE ENZO HAS NONE' · MEADEN: 'NOT ENOUGH TO DO OTHER THAN HANG ON TIGHT…' · 'FASTEST WAS NOT THE FAVOURITE' = OUR SUMMARY

scenes.text: And yet, the car's value has overtaken what most of its contemporaries have earned. Sports Car Market wrote in two thousand eighteen that the number of Enzos does not grow while the number of supercar collectors does. That is an analyst's view, and the same analyst said buyers would not do as well as the seller, a forecast that has so far been wrong.
scenes.caption: SCM (2018): 'THE NUMBER OF ENZOS DOESN'T [GROW]' WHILE COLLECTORS DO · 'NEW OWNER WILL NOT DO NEARLY AS WELL' → HAGERTY TODAY +42% vs 2018 SALE (3,600,000 ÷ 2,530,774, OUR ARITHMETIC) · 'WRONG SO FAR' = OUR OBSERVATION

scenes.text: Motor Trend Classic's ranking of the Enzo as the fourth greatest Ferrari, and Sports Car International's third place for the decade, are from Wikipedia. Neither is dated beyond the page. Jalopnik argued the Enzo would not draw design complaints if introduced today. As a story about taste, the Enzo went from controversial to collectible within about two decades.
scenes.caption: WIKIPEDIA: MOTOR TREND CLASSIC #4 GREATEST FERRARIS (UNDATED) · SPORTS CAR INTERNATIONAL #3 (2004) · BLOOMBERG BUSINESSWEEK 'UGLIEST' (UNDATED) · JALOPNIK 2010 · 'ABOUT TWO DECADES' ≈ 2002 → 2026 = 24 YEARS (OUR ARITHMETIC; 'CONTROVERSIAL' PER BLOOMBERG LIST, 'COLLECTIBLE' PER RM)

scenes.text: So here is the story in order. A hypercar that followed an unloved predecessor, built with technology Formula One banned, sold by invitation to chosen owners, with a four hundredth car for a Pope. Its numbers are argued over to this day: nought to sixty, top speed, production, even the charity. The one thing everyone agrees on is that it is now very valuable.
scenes.caption: F50 (UNLOVED) → ENZO 2002 · ACTIVE AERO F1 BANNED · INVITE-ONLY 349 → 399 → 400 · POPE'S CAR · DISPUTED: 0–60, TOP SPEED, PRODUCTION (400 / 498), CHARITY · HAGERTY TODAY $3.6 M

scenes.text: Even the car's dimensions disagree. Wikipedia lists the Enzo's wheelbase as twenty-six fifty millimetres. RM Sotheby's London page says twenty-six forty-nine, and its Arizona page says one hundred four point four inches, which by our arithmetic is twenty-six fifty-two millimetres. All are within three millimetres, so the disagreement is rounding, but it shows how the same car gets written up differently.
scenes.caption: WIKIPEDIA: 2,650 MM · RM (LONDON 2014): 2,649 MM · RM (ARIZONA 2017): 104.4 IN = 2,651.8 MM (OUR ARITHMETIC) · SPREAD 3 MM → ROUNDING
scenes.chapter: The details that do not match

scenes.text: Weight is more serious. Wikipedia gives twelve fifty-five kilograms dry and fourteen eighty curb. Evo's table says twelve fifty-five dry, and does not give the curb figure. By our arithmetic, the difference between the dry and curb weights is two hundred twenty-five kilograms, or eighteen percent, though the page does not itemise what accounts for the difference.
scenes.caption: WIKIPEDIA: 1,255 KG DRY · 1,480 KG CURB · EVO: 1,255 KG DRY · 1,480 − 1,255 = 225 KG (17.9%) (OUR ARITHMETIC) · BREAKDOWN OF THE DIFFERENCE: NOT ITEMISED

scenes.text: Acceleration shows the same pattern. Wikipedia lists zero to one hundred sixty-one kilometres an hour, a hundred miles an hour, in six point six seconds for the Enzo and eight point five for the F50. By our arithmetic, the Enzo was twenty-two percent quicker to that speed, a bigger gap than the fraction of a second that separated them to sixty.
scenes.caption: WIKIPEDIA: 0–161 KM/H (100 MPH) — ENZO 6.6 S · F50 8.5 S · 1 − 6.6 ÷ 8.5 = 22.4% QUICKER (OUR ARITHMETIC) · 0–60: 3.14 / 3.3 vs 3.8 S

scenes.text: Evo's table for the Enzo says six hundred fifty-one brake horsepower and a price of about four hundred twenty thousand pounds in two thousand two, with a value today of one point six to two point six million pounds. Sports Car Market's list price is six hundred forty-three thousand three hundred thirty dollars. We have no exchange-rate source, so we cannot say whether the two prices describe the same car.
scenes.caption: EVO: c.£420,000 (2002); VALUE TODAY £1.6–2.6 M (ONLINE EDITION 23 OCT 2024) · SCM: $643,330 · GEARSHIFTERS (UNSOURCED): $650,000 / $659,330 · NO EXCHANGE-RATE SOURCE

scenes.text: The first owners' cars give a feel for the era. RM Sotheby's London page describes a one-owner car delivered in Italy with just under nineteen hundred kilometres, certified by Ferrari Classiche and recently serviced at Graypaul Nottingham. Sports Car Market's twenty eighteen car had under sixty-one hundred kilometres, one owner, and a sixteen thousand dollar service. Both were driven very little.
scenes.caption: RM (LONDON 2014): ONE OWNER, <1,900 KM, CLASSICHE, SERVICED GRAYPAUL NOTTINGHAM, BUILT 2003, DELIVERED IN ITALY · SCM (2018): <6,100 KM FROM NEW, ONE OWNER, ABOUT 4,000 MILES AT SALE, $16,000 SERVICE · 6,100 KM = 3,790 MI (OUR ARITHMETIC; SCM'S TWO MILEAGES DIFFER)

scenes.text: Sports Car Market's own mileage figures don't match. It says less than sixty-one hundred kilometres from new, which is about thirty-eight hundred miles, and also about four thousand miles at sale. By our arithmetic, the two differ by two hundred miles, five percent. The article does not explain, and the gap is small, but it is one more example of numbers that don't line up.
scenes.caption: SCM: '<6,100 KM' (= 3,790 MI) vs 'ABOUT 4,000 MILES' · 4,000 − 3,790 = 210 MI (5.2%) (OUR ARITHMETIC) · REASON: NOT STATED (ROUNDING?)

scenes.text: The price sequence is not smooth. By our arithmetic, the September twenty eighteen London sale was six percent below the Arizona sale a year earlier, then the August twenty twenty-four Mecum result was thirteen percent above the London one. Different cars, different mileage and different venues all matter. From the twenty fifteen California result to Hagerty's value, the average rise is about six percent a year.
scenes.caption: RM ARIZONA 2017 $2,695,000 → SCM LONDON SEP 2018 $2,530,774 = −6.1% · → MECUM AUG 2024 $2,860,000 = +13.0% · RM CA15 $1,870,000 → HAGERTY $3,600,000 = 1.93× OVER ~11 YEARS = 6.1%/YR (OUR ARITHMETIC; DIFFERENT CARS)

scenes.text: So this is how the Enzo's story reads in the numbers. A car sold by invitation at about six hundred forty thousand dollars, with a Pope's example selling for one point one million. A decade later, two to two and a half million dollars. And now, three and a half million or more. The price of the story keeps rising, even as the facts about the car remain disputed.
scenes.caption: LIST $643,330 (SCM) → 400TH CAR $1.1 M (WIKIPEDIA) → $1.87–2.70 M (2015–2018) → $3.6 M (HAGERTY TODAY) · 'THREE AND A HALF MILLION OR MORE' = HAGERTY $3.6 M, SOME ESTIMATES HIGHER · 'FACTS DISPUTED' = SEE CONFLICTS ABOVE

scenes.text: The Enzo was followed by the LaFerrari. Italpassion says one LaFerrari offered at RM Sotheby's Phoenix, one of four hundred ninety-nine produced and delivered new in California, has a 6.3 litre V12 with a hybrid system making nine hundred forty-nine horsepower combined. By our arithmetic, that is forty-six percent more than the Enzo's six hundred fifty-one, and the production total is almost exactly the Enzo's four hundred.
scenes.caption: ITALPASSION (RM PHOENIX, 23 JAN 2026, LOT 177): LAFERRARI — 1 OF 499, DELIVERED NEW IN CALIFORNIA, 1,938 MI, 6.3 L V12 + HYBRID, 949 HP COMBINED · 949 ÷ 651 = +45.8% (OUR ARITHMETIC) · 499 vs 400/498 ENZOS

scenes.text: That LaFerrari's estimate was four and a half to five million dollars, Italpassion says, below the five to six million for the low-mileage Enzo on the same sale. By our arithmetic, the Enzo estimate is at least eleven percent higher. So in this one sale, the older, naturally aspirated car was expected to outprice its hybrid successor. Results are not in our sources.
scenes.caption: ITALPASSION: LAFERRARI EST. $4.5–5 M · ENZO EST. $5–6 M · 5.0 ÷ 4.5 = +11.1% · 6.0 ÷ 5.0 = +20% (OUR ARITHMETIC) · ENZO HAS 746 MI vs LAFERRARI 1,938 MI · RESULTS: NOT IN OUR SOURCES

scenes.text: SCM's description of the Enzo as the ultimate iteration of the naturally aspirated, limited-edition Ferrari hypercar sums up why. It also listed the Bugatti Veyron, Porsche nine eighteen and McLaren P one as alternatives for buyers. Those are the cars that followed it. Whether the Enzo's special status holds as hybrids take over is a prediction that we cannot source.
scenes.caption: SCM (2018): 'THE ULTIMATE ITERATION OF THE NATURALLY ASPIRATED, LIMITED-EDITION FERRARI HYPERCAR' · ALTERNATIVES: VEYRON, 918, P1 · FUTURE OF NA STATUS: PREDICTION, NOT IN OUR SOURCES

scenes.text: What we could not confirm: whether Schumacher worked on the Enzo; the date the Pope received his car, and who bought it; the true production total; which charity benefited; the Enzo's true top speed; and what the Enzo's mules cost to build. And where Hagerty's record and Italpassion's differ, we do not know which is right. We flagged each one.
